newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares continue slow-motion slide.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares continue slow-motion slide.

text.p: Italian shares closed mostly lower on Wednesday as the bourse continued its slow-motion slide after last month's sharp gains with nervousness about Italy's EMU prospects also weighing on sentiment.

The all-share mibtel index finished 0.64 percent lower at 12,160 while the the blue chip mib30 closed 0.43 percent down at 18,133. Dealers said Wall Street's weak opening further dampened the mood with volumes dominated by intra-day trading.

Foreign and domestic funds were mostly sidelined. Some traders attributed the market's weak performance more to technical factors rather than fears that the government might have trouble pushing through a supplementary budget.

"The market has probably got at least another five percent to lose. It has only lost about two percent so far this week and while it was rising it was gaining by up to three percent each day," said a Milan broker.

Energy group ENI was stable, gaining 0.52 percent to 8,969 lire, while auto maker Fiat advanced 1.01 percent to 5,098 lire. But telecom stocks took another battering, Stet easing 1.9 percent to 7,890 lire and Telecom Italia falling 1.02 percent to 4,373 lire.
BCI was the only bright light among the banks, closing 2.74 percent higher at 3,606 lire while Credito closed almost unchanged and all other major banks beat a retreat.
